title: Stable Binding Chooser with Latency Profile Lens
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Provide a lightweight console surface for engineering teams to choose a model version binding (stable binding) for a route and immediately inspect published performance profiles (latency / p99 / throughput) aligned to that binding. The UI should make trade-offs explicit (latency vs cost vs quality), show recent rollouts that used the binding, and let users publish an optional binding note. This feature reduces accidental regression risk during fast rollouts and speeds up manual pin operations for platform teams.
motivation: Customers frequently ask for a faster way to bind routes to specific model versions while understanding the runtime implications. Current flows require jumping between the model catalog, a separate profiling view, and the route editor. We want a single chooser surface with an embedded latency profile lens and rollout history so pinning is a single cohesive action.
success_metrics: Decrease post-pin performance regressions detected by alerts by 25% within 30 days
>70% of manual pins created via the new surface within 6 weeks of release
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to pick a stable model binding for the payments route and see expected p50/p95/p99 latencies so I can avoid regressions
As an SRE, I want to compare two candidate versions side-by-side and see their throughput and cost estimate so I can choose the lower-risk option
As a product manager, I want to attach a short note and reference to the binding to capture why this version was chosen
scope_in: Chooser surface embedded in route editor (right rail modal)
Latency profile lens showing time-series p50/p95/p99 and recent perf snapshots
Side-by-side micro-comparison for up to 2 versions
Attachment of a brief binding note and optional rollback TTL
Telemetry events for pin creation and profile view
scope_out: Automated canary rollout orchestration (handled by separate release automation)
In-depth model evals or token-level diffs
Multi-version traffic split UI (not just single stable binding)
acceptance_criteria: Chooser surface is reachable from route editor and opens within 200ms
Latency lens fetches and renders last 7 days of p50/p95/p99 for selected versions
Pin action records telemetry and creates a binding note visible in route metadata
Side-by-side comparison correctly shows throughput and cost estimate computed by Optimize service
E2E test covering pin creation and rollback TTL behavior
tasks: Design: finalize mobile-responsive layout and microcopy
Frontend: implement chooser modal and latency lens component
Backend: expose aggregated profile API for N-day windows
Optimize: add cost estimate endpoint for candidate versions
QA: create e2e tests and perf budgets
Docs: console help article and release notes
decisions: Render latency lens as an area+line chart to emphasize tail behavior (decided 2026-02-24)
Limit side-by-side to two versions to keep mental load small (trade-off: multi-compare deferred)
Cost estimate will be a rough order-of-magnitude derived from Optimize service rather than exact billing (to avoid billing coupling)
blockers: Backend aggregated profile endpoint currently in RFC (runtime team needs 2 sprints)
Cost estimate integration requires Optimize API v1.3 stabilization
